audit.whatIsWrong: Four fields tell you to stun Rumble out of Flamespitter: whys[1] 'stun him inside the Flamespitter channel before he overheats', the Level 2-3 spike 'stun Rumble mid-Flamespitter cast', the early prose 'W-stun him mid-channel so the overheat damage never completes', and wants.you[0] 'W-stun him mid-Flamespitter channel to end the overheat window'.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Rumble torches opponents in front of him, dealing magic damage in a cone for 3 seconds.' It is not flagged as a channel and there is nothing in the kit file to suggest CC ends it - it burns for its duration whether he is stunned or not. This is the kind of error that makes a player refuse a trade she actually wins, because she thinks the stun failed. The rumble__riven mirror found the identical phrasing in four places on the other side, so the string has been copied around.
audit.corrected: All four fields now say the stun buys the rest of your combo rather than switching the cone off.

audit.whatIsWrong: Scrap Shield is the matchup's designated tracked cooldown - it is focus.text, it is the loading-screen line, it is dosFull[0], and whys[3] says in as many words 'His Scrap Shield cooldown is your commit timer'. The mid prose tells you to watch for the moment it drops.
audit.why: Scrap Shield is on a flat 6-second cooldown. There is no window: by the time you have closed the gap it is back. Building the whole commit plan on it means waiting for something that never happens. The resource that actually gates Rumble is Heat - at 50% he enters Danger Zone and every basic ability is empowered, and at 100% he Overheats and cannot cast spells at all. That is the real commit window and it appears nowhere in the matchup.
audit.corrected: whys[3], the mid prose and wants.you[2] rewritten around the Heat bar and the Overheat lockout.

audit.whatIsWrong: The mid prose says 'Rumble places it as a wall, not as a reactive trade tool — dash over or around it with E', describing Flamespitter.
audit.why: Flamespitter is a 600-unit cone in front of Rumble, not a placed zone; the ability that is placed as a wall is The Equalizer, at 1750 range. Telling a player to dash 'over' a cone attached to the enemy's facing produces the wrong movement entirely - the answer to a cone is to get behind or beside its owner, and the answer to a wall is to cross it.
audit.corrected: Mid prose rewritten to describe the cone correctly and the late prose to name The Equalizer as the wall.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Skill, Rumble, Rumble, Skill, Skill, Rumble, Rumble while the packet chart reads Skill, Riven, Riven, Riven, Riven, Riven, Skill and Riven wins 54.61%.
audit.why: The page hands Rumble four stages while every one of its own whys says the opposite: whys[1] calls Level 2 'your first real all-in threat', whys[2] says 'he has no escape from the Q chain', whys[3] says to bank the HP lead, whys[4] says to force the all-in, whys[5] says to finish the kill. Only whys[6] is genuinely two-sided, which matches the packet's Skill at two items. Six of seven rows contradict the prose beneath them.
audit.corrected: Rows 1 through 6 flipped as one atomic paired group in both layers to Skill, Riven, Riven, Riven, Riven, Riven, Skill, with ratings moved to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: The matchup's stated win condition is 'build MR', and nothing anywhere says Rumble removes it.
audit.why: Electro Harpoon reduces Magic Resist, carries two charges and comes back every half second between them at 850 range. So the poke that reads as harmless chip is also stripping the exact stat the page tells you to buy, and each harpoon makes the following Flamespitter hit harder. A player who buys Mercury's Treads and stands in poke range is undoing the purchase.
audit.corrected: The shred written into whys[4], the mid prose and wants.foe[1].

edits.before: W online means you can stun him inside the Flamespitter channel before he overheats — your first real all-in threat arrives a full level before his kit comes together.
edits.after: Ki Burst arrives on 11s and he has no dash to answer it — your first real all-in threat lands a level before his kit comes together, though the stun will not stop Flamespitter.

edits.after: Scrap Shield is a 6-second cooldown and never really down — the Heat bar is your commit timer, and Overheat locks his casts.

edits.before: Blade of the Exile extends your melee range past the Flamespitter burn edge and Wind Slash executes him through Scrap Shield HP — force the all-in when his E-harpoon is on cooldown.
edits.after: Blade of the Exile reaches past Flamespitter's 600-unit cone and Wind Slash executes through Scrap Shield HP — force the all-in once both Electro Harpoon charges are spent.

edits.before: Immortal Shieldbow lets you absorb the Equalizer DoT tick while closing distance — bait the R cast, dash in after the first wave passes, and finish the kill on long cooldowns.
edits.after: Immortal Shieldbow absorbs The Equalizer's burn while you close the gap — bait the cast, cross the flame line, and finish him while a 130-second ultimate is gone.

edits.before: W online at 2 lets you stun Rumble mid-Flamespitter cast — full Q-W-E combo before he can overheat ends the trade decisively.
edits.after: Ki Burst online at 2 on an 11-second cooldown — Flamespitter burns on regardless, so the stun buys your combo rather than an interrupt.

edits.before: At Level 1 Rumble wants to walk up and angle Flamespitter across your body while you last-hit — respect it and stay at Q-tip range rather than auto-trading into the channel. The moment W comes online at Level 2, the dynamic flips completely: step into his Flamespitter, burn your E to tank the first tick, and W-stun him mid-channel so the overheat damage never completes. He has no reliable gap-close or escape, so a clean E-in, W-stun, Q chain kills his trade pattern entirely. At Level 3 you have the full combo — lead with Q1 to close distance, bait the E-harpoon on your shield, then re-engage with Q2-W-Q3 after it passes. He cannot match your burst in a short window before his next Flamespitter rotation.
edits.after: At Level 1 Rumble wants to walk up and angle Flamespitter across your body while you last-hit — respect it and stay at Broken Wings range rather than auto-trading into the cone. The moment Ki Burst comes online at Level 2 the dynamic flips: step in, spend Valor to eat the first tick, and land the stun. Do not expect it to switch Flamespitter off — the cone burns for its full three seconds either way; what the stun buys is the rest of your combo landing while he cannot walk out of it. He has no gap-close and no escape, so Valor in, Ki Burst, Broken Wings chain beats his pattern outright. At Level 3, lead with Q1, bait a harpoon onto the shield, then re-engage with Q2, stun, Q3.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are straightforward if you respect one thing: never walk through a pre-cast Flamespitter zone. Rumble places it as a wall, not as a reactive trade tool — dash over or around it with E, then immediately W-stun him so he cannot reposition into overheat range. His Scrap Shield gives some sustain and move speed but the cooldown is visible; the moment it drops, that is your commit window. At Level 6 your Blade of the Exile first cast extends your melee range beyond the outer edge of Flamespitter, letting you Q chain him without standing fully inside the burn. Save Wind Slash until he is below half HP — the execute damage at that threshold is a clean kill through whatever Scrap Shield HP he has banked.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are straightforward if you respect one thing: Flamespitter is a 600-unit cone in front of him, so the answer is to be beside or behind him, not to wait it out. Do not plan around Scrap Shield either — it is a flat 6-second cooldown and effectively always up. Watch the Heat bar instead: at 50% he is in Danger Zone and every ability is empowered, and at 100% he Overheats and cannot cast at all, which is your real commit window. Electro Harpoon carries two charges and shreds magic resist, so poke that looks harmless is also making the next Flamespitter hurt more. At 6, Blade of the Exile reaches past the cone's edge; hold Wind Slash for below half HP.

edits.before: By first-item completion Rumble's Equalizer becomes his equaliser — one well-placed R along your intended dash path punishes a careless engage and burns through your shielding over several seconds. Never dash in a straight line toward him in a teamfight or side-lane skirmish when his R is available; bait it with a feigned engage, let the lava channel tick down, then close in with E and W-stun while he is on long cooldowns. Two items in you remain a real threat in the 1v1, but his teamfight AOE can swing 5v5s badly, so prioritise converting your lane lead into turrets and neutral objectives rather than banking on solo-killing him repeatedly once he has Liandry's stacked.
edits.after: By first-item completion The Equalizer is his real answer — 1750 units of flame wall laid across your dash path, punishing a careless engage and burning through your shielding over several seconds. Never dash in a straight line toward him in a teamfight or side skirmish while it is up; bait it with a feigned engage, cross the line rather than standing on it, then close with Valor and Ki Burst while a 130-second ultimate is gone. Two items in you remain a real threat in the 1v1, but his teamfight zoning can swing 5v5s badly, so convert your lane lead into turrets and neutral objectives rather than banking on repeat solo kills once he has Liandry's stacked.

notes: Packet suspectNames: 'His Scrap Shield' is a FALSE POSITIVE (correct name with a possessive). 'Save Equalizer' is a real if minor one - the ability is The Equalizer - and I corrected it. The 'interrupts your Flamespitter channel' error appears here in four fields and the rumble__riven mirror found the same phrasing four times on the other side, so it is a copied string that likely leaked into other Rumble matchups outside this slice; worth a grep. The most useful structural finding is that the matchup's designated tracked cooldown is a 6-second ability: Scrap Shield is focus.text, the loading line, dosFull[0] and the stated commit timer in whys[3], and it is never meaningfully down. The full layer still points the player at it in focus.text, breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.mid, the loading line and report[5], all of which carry mojibake em-dashes so I left them for an encoding-safe pass - but the tracked ability for this matchup should be changed to Heat / Overheat, which is a champion-level decision I flagged rather than made. FLAG: the kit file gives Scrap Shield knockup and terrain flags, but Riot's description is a shield plus a burst of speed and nothing else; I wrote no displacement claim, which also means the _missing-interactions 'both sides carry displacement' rule for this pair looks like a flag-parsing artefact rather than a real interaction.
